text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, giving back some of Friday's gains after hitting a three-week high of $137.20 on Tuesday. The pullback reflects mixed signals in oil markets: while U.S. crude held steady around $91.50, global crude prices edged higher to $96, but the company faced headwinds from geopolitical developments that could actually weaken near-term oil demand—specifically the new Trump administration deal to restore Venezuelan oil production, which would add supply to global markets over time and potentially cap price gains that have benefited the stock.

The broader energy sector is caught between two opposing forces. On one hand, refinery disruptions in Russia and Ukraine, plus the EU's formal entry into Iran sanctions and U.S. military efforts to secure shipping lanes, have pushed diesel to record highs and kept crude relatively firm. On the other hand, the Venezuela supply agreement signals a shift toward pragmatism over geopolitical conflict, which could mean more stable but lower-priced oil ahead—a scenario that pressures integrated oil companies like ConocoPhillips even as it stabilizes energy markets.
